narration: Given multi-temporal inputs x-tau and x-tau-prime, a shared-weight Patch Feature Extractor with a Deformable Transformer Encoder extracts structured patch representations z-s-tau and z-s-tau-prime.
In parallel, the Patch Matching Network processes both temporal frames to estimate cross-temporal correspondences and guide patch matching.
The Multi-Temporal Patch Matching module aligns feature tokens across time frames, establishing semantic correspondences between matching patches.
Based on matching scores, the model selects positive and negative patch sets z-tau-plus, z-tau-prime-plus, and z-tau-prime-minus to form contrastive pairs.
The Object Residual Module subtracts learned object prototypes phi-k from patch representations to isolate fine-grained view and scale variations.
Finally, the computed residual representations are supervised jointly by multi-view loss and scale-regression loss to optimize multi-temporal representation learning.
